note: Spread of annual returns. In the identity refunds are netted in g, so sigma acts only through the refund cap and the fill years (not reachable). Direction: a higher sigma raises the arithmetic mean over the geometric g (+0.34 points of return at the central 8.2%, my arithmetic) and the loss-year share.
Loss-year share. Acts through refunds, the cap on them and the reserve fill (P1, P4). Not reachable on the identity. Direction: more loss years, larger refunds, longer fill.
Longest loss run. Acts on the reserve fill and on P3 only. Not reachable. Direction: a longer run lengthens the transition.
Gap between the end of the return history and the last full year. A data-vintage input; no term in the identity.
Share of adults at or above W_min. Sets the number of payers and M2b; omega depends on the wealth share I-D4c, not on the head count.
